Probe evidence implies irs.gov serves a real robots.txt: the Form 15620 probe notes "/dmaf is not disallowed by irs.gov robots.txt", and the app-host probe refers to "the irs.gov content robots.txt". However, the application host that runs the EIN online assistant (sa.www4.irs.gov) returned HTTP 503 for robots.txt. So an agent cannot learn its permissions there before fetching. Missing for 10: a direct probe or citation of the irs.gov robots.txt and its contents, a stable robots.txt on the application hosts (sa.www4.irs.gov), and evidence that the rules cover the transactional flows an agent would actually use.

The IRS publishes some delegation rules. A third-party designee may apply for an EIN with signed authorization from the responsible party (irs-supp-13). It defines a credentialed Authorized e-file Provider role with an enrollment and suitability path (irs-supp-5, irs-supp-6). It also states that signed mobile-friendly forms, including the 83(b) Form 15620, require the taxpayer's own Online Account behind ID.me biometric proofing, which marks those signatures as personal (irs-supp-12, irs-supp-9). This is scattered across individual services rather than one published map of what third parties may and may not do. Missing for 10: general power-of-attorney and authorization forms (e.g. representative or tax-information authorizations), a consolidated catalog of third-party roles and their scopes, explicit designee form details, and independent corroboration.

The IRS publishes an exact paper/fax fallback for the EIN flow, which matters because the online assistant keeps limited hours: mail or fax Form SS-4 to 'Internal Revenue Service, Attn: EIN Operation, Cincinnati, OH 45999, Fax: 855-641-6935'. It also documents a paper rail for the 83(b) election (a written statement or Form 15620 filed with the Service Center). Missing for 10: an exact address for the 83(b) paper filing (evidence only says 'the Service Center where you file your return'), and independent or hands-on confirmation that the mail/fax rails complete the task.

Missing for 10: API coverage of EIN application, Online Account, transcripts, payments and signed forms such as Form 15620, a public documented API spec, and self-serve API access.
